title: 航空宇宙工学入門とキャリアデザイン
subtitle: Introduction to Aerospace Engineering and Career Design
keywords: Manufacturing and engineering 2.Aeronautics and Astronautics 3.Mechanisms of Aircraft and Spacecraft 4.Technologies Related to Aircraft and Spacecraft 5.Career Design
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn about current and future technologies supporting the modern world. (2) learn to think for oneself. (3) establish a learning posture conducive to developing their future career. (4) learn to think about the essence of phenomena and objects and to think about things logically. (5) learn the ability to design in their major engineering field.
advice: This is an introduction to engineering as it relates to aeronautics and astronautics. The objectives of this subject are shown below. 1. Understanding of the system of the Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics 2. Understanding the Role of Aircraft and Spacecraft-Related Technologies in Society 3. Obtaining the ability to investigate the essence of phenomena and objects through suitable exercises 4. Introduction to the research field 5. General exercises Students should learn the relationship between engineering and society and the role of engineers. Student should understand the importance of basic knowledge and attain a self-driven attitude toward learning in the department of aeronautics and astronautics. The level of students’ achievement will be evaluated through reports and presentations with a view of their ability to convert their knowledge into practice.
requiredKnowledge: Selection of an area of interest in engineering Attitude of autonomy It is also important to utilize AI and open data as assistance to own learning.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the role of the engineering departmentand prepare one’s own learning plan.
Be able to consider future learning methods and plan to apply them.
Be able to briefly explain overview of aircraft and spacecraft.
Be able to briefly explain an overview of aircraft and spacecraft-related technologies.
Be able to briefly explain an overview of the history of aircraft and spacecraft.
Be able to describe one’s own carrier-building process and to explain it to others.
